answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via seismic time-of-arrival verification. Nodes prove geographic separation by recording low-frequency ground pulses propagated across diverse terrain, such as a tidal inlet, a knoll, or an elevated terrace. An attacker cannot compute subsurface acoustic dispersion remotely and must deploy physical geophone hardware per identity. However, background seismic noise from traffic or tremors distorts arrival times, leading to false rejections.
